doc.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Playing in the studio versus a gig
summary: Caine tries to play in tune and underplay on records; the depends on the project, such as Connick's.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Is playing in the studio, making a record, how is it different from playing a gig?

Well I try to play more in tune, I try to be more conscious of playing in tune. You know it’s tough, it depends man. That’s a good question because I always used to, I still approach it some — when I go in the studio if I’m making a record, it depends on the recording but I always try to underplay. You know I try to play the right thing you know. But I would try to err on the side of underplaying, playing more simpler, not overplaying, not playing a bunch of dumb stuff you know, because it would — but as I’ve gotten older, now I just kind of go in and hit hard and wish it well. I mean it depends on the scenario I guess. Like if I’m doing a Harry Connick record that’s going to be really — something that has to be really clean you know, it depends on, it kind of depends on the situation. But ultimately it shouldn’t really affect you at all. You should just go — you should just go hit it.
Yeah. You have records that you’ve been on that, well first of all do you listen to the records that you’ve played on?
